title.narrative: % of participants who report there are fewer climaterelated conflicts in their community than 12 months ago

description.narrative: Definition: Climaterelated conflict any conflict over access to diminishing natural resources which have likely been impacted by climate change (e.g. water, arable land, pasture land). Community: The village in which the respondent lives. The conflict could be between two or more communities and still counted if the respondent lives in one of the communities involved in the conflict. Reference period is 12 months (one year) prior to when the survey takes place. Participants should be asked to recall the situation 12 months prior compared to the day of the survey. Calculation: Numerator number of survey respondents reporting there are fewer climaterelated conflicts than 12 months ago. Denominator number of survey respondents interviewed in the catchment area.

title.narrative: Output 1.1: Key members of communities and statelevel institutions have increased peacebuilding and social cohesion knowledge and skills

description.narrative: Output 1.1: Key members of communities and statelevel institutions have increased peacebuilding and social cohesion knowledge and skillsOutput 1.1: Key members of communities and statelevel institutions have increased peacebuilding and social cohesion knowledge and skills

title.narrative: % of participants who demonstrate Functional or Full Competency in peacebuilding & social cohesion

description.narrative: Definition: Based on whether each participant does or does not show each of the behavioral evidences listed for each competency, a value of 1 for yes or a value of 0 for no is assigned. Their overall competency level is calculated by taking a simple average of the values given for each of the behavioral evidences for each competency. Using the calculated rate for each participant, respondents are classified in four levels of competency as follows: Basic: (0 <40%), In Development: (40 <60%), Functionally Competent: (60 <75%), Fully Competent: (75 100%). To count the number of participants who have reached at least a functional level of module 1 of the SMART skills manual, Organizational Competencies, which includes good governance, transformative and participative leadership, learning/adaptation for good performance, and effective networking/negotiation/advocacy. A simple average of the score for each competency 16 is calculated. Participants who reach at least a qualification of 60% or more count for the indicator as having reached at least a functional level of the competency. Calculation: Numerator number of participants reaching at least 60% for peacebuilding and social cohesion competencies per definition above. Denominator total surveyed participants of peacebuilding and social cohesion trainings for communities and statelevel institutions. Disaggregation by age group, sex, and participant type (community vs. statelevel institution)

comment.narrative: 0 was entered at baseline as a placeholder. baseline competency levels will be measured prior to trainings as each training is administered to project participants so this value is not yet available to report on.

title.narrative: Project participants perception of formal and informal institutions approach to addressing conflict and climaterelated risks

description.narrative: Formal institutions government institutions, officially registered local organizations Informal institutions communitybased groups or local organizations that are not officially registered. Climaterelated risks floods, drought, or other weather conditions that impact households livelihoods and wellbeing. Qualitative data will be analyzed to identify key themes and patterns in participants perceptions and disaggregated by sex and age group.

comment.narrative: A complete lack of contribution from the government emerged as a common sentiment throughout the FGDs. A widespread belief that the government is not fulfilling its role is likely to affect trust and willingness to engage with future government initiatives. Although the majority of respondents had a lot of trust for the traditional leaders there were two instances in the FGD when respondents reported that the sheikhs did not distribute the aid they received from an NGO equitably and were unwilling to represent womens interests when acting as a focal point with NGOs . This suggest that while establishing good relationships with traditional leaders is instrumental for ensuring the success of the project a system of oversight and direct accessible channels of communication with the implementor is necessary to ensure that the needs of all people in the community are served equitably.

title.narrative: reduced Coping Strategy Index

description.narrative: Definition: The rCSI is based on a list of five foodrelated coping strategies: 1. Rely on less preferred and less expensive foods, 2. Borrow food or rely on help from friends or relatives, 3. Limit portion size at mealtime, 4. Restrict consumption by adults in order for small children to eat, 5. Reduce the number of meals eaten in a day. Frequency of each strategy is reported as how many days over the last 7 days the coping strategy was used by any member of the household. Calculation: The rCSI raw scores are calculated by multiplying the frequency with which a behavior was used in the last 7 days by any member of the household by the severity weight, then summing the weighted scores for each coping strategy. Both the mean and median are reported, along with the 95% CI and std. Mean Add all of the raw score values from all beneficiaries included in the survey then divide by the total number of beneficiaries included in the survey. Median Arrange the observations in order from least to greatest value. If there are an odd number of observations, the median is the middle value. If there is an even number of observations, the median is the average of the two middle values. Disaggregated by sex of head of HH.

comment.narrative: Mean 20.1 95 CI 19.2 21.1 Median 19.0 standard deviation 8.14 n 288Mean of male headed households 19.5 Mean of female headed households 21.4
target is decrease in the mean rCSI from baseline to endline mean index of 14 is based on prior assessments from other CRS resilience projects implemented in similar areas
